items.title: Mahalia Jackson Interview, 1955-07-26
items.q: And of course, we, um, we got a chance to, uh, to hear more of Bessie Smith. And I suppose basically, uh, that's why so many people say that, uh, I sound like Bessie Smith, but, uh, I suppose I do.

ctx.x: these things are done. Tell me, I've read somewhere that Bessie Smith

has meant something to you. Well, uh, in the South, in New Orleans where I was born, I didn't get a chance to hear, uh, the great singers like Roland Hayes and, and, um, uh, Grace Moore, Lily Pond, and all those great singers until I came to Chicago up north. Well, we, we did have a chance to hear the blues down there because it's the type of thing that you can hear in the South as soon as you get off the train. People in the South have the, uh, radios or the old-time phonograph just as loud and you can hear the…
But you wouldn't say that you have learned, uh, directly from listening to her. No, no, because
